1.note: Isaiah is speaking of Yahweh coming down from the sky as if Yahweh would **rend the heavens** like a piece of fabric. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you would split open the sky and come through]
Here, **your face** represents “your presence.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [From your presence]

2.note: Isaiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. He is saying that fire causes brushwood to burn and also causes water to boil. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [As fire kindles brushwood, as fire boils water]

Here, the word **to** marks **to make your name known to your adversaries** as the goal or purpose of what Yahweh would do. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose.

2.q: כִּ⁠קְדֹ֧חַ אֵ֣שׁ הֲמָסִ֗ים מַ֚יִם תִּבְעֶה אֵ֔שׁ
2.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **fire kindles brushwood** and **fire boils water** with powerful, visible effect, so Yahweh’s presence would powerfully affect the nations and make them tremble. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [Just as fire powerfully consumes brushwood and boils water]
Here, **your name** represents “your reputation.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [your reputation]

3.note: Here the phrase **from your face** could: (1) be a common expression of the culture that means “on your account” or “on your behalf,” Alternate translation: [on your behalf] or (2) represent “from your presence.” Alternate translation: [from before you]

4.note: The pronoun **they** refers to people in general. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [people have not heard, people have not listened]

Isaiah is using **an eye** to represent a whole person who sees. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [no one has seen]

Even though Isaiah is addressing God directly, he is speaking of him in the third person as **he works for the one waiting for him** to show respect. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in a respectful form in the second person. Alternate translation: [you work for the one waiting for you]

5.note: Isaiah is not referring to a specific person with **the one rejoicing and doing righteousness**. He means people who do this in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [those who rejoice and do righteousness]

Isaiah is speaking of the manner of life that Yahweh requires as if it were **ways**, or paths, that people walk in. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [as they live as you require]

Isaiah is using the term **Behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Indeed]

Isaiah repeats the pronoun **you** for emphasis, stressing that it was indeed Yahweh who was angry. If a speaker of your language would use a repeated or explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing this emphasis. Alternate translation: [it was indeed you who were angry]

The pronoun **them** refers to the **ways** of Yahweh, which are mentioned earlier in the verse. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [for we had sinned against your ways]

Isaiah is using the question form to express doubt about whether the people can be saved, since Yahweh has been angry at their sin. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [so surely we cannot be saved]

The expression **be saved** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [so will you save us]

6.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **the unclean** are ceremonially defiled and unacceptable, so the people who are speaking here have become unacceptable to Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [like people who are ceremonially defiled and rejected]

Isaiah is using the adjective **unclean** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [like an unclean person]

The point of this comparison is that just as **a menstrual rag** is unclean and worthless, so are **all of our righteousnesses**, the good deeds the people have done. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and all of our righteousnesses are unclean and worthless]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **righteousnesses**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [all the righteous things we do]

7.note: Isaiah is using **calling on your name** as a common expression of the culture to mean “worshiping you and praying to you.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [worshiping and praying to you]

Isaiah is using **awakening himself to hold onto you** as a common expression of the culture to mean “rousing himself to remain devoted to you.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [stirring himself to stay committed to you]

The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [Because]

Isaiah is using **you have hidden your face from us** as a common expression of the culture to mean “you have withdrawn your favor and help from us.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you have withdrawn your help from us]

Isaiah is speaking of Yahweh causing the people to lose all their courage as if he had **melted** them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you have caused us to lose our courage]

Here, **hand** represents the power or control that the people’s iniquities have over them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [through the power of our iniquities]

8.note: Isaiah is speaking of Yahweh as if he were the people’s **Father**, because Yahweh created them and cares for them as a father cares for his children. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you are like a father to us]

Isaiah is speaking of Yahweh and the people as if Yahweh were a **potter** and the people were the **clay** that he shapes, because Yahweh formed them and has authority over them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You formed us and have authority over us]

9.note: Isaiah is using **remember iniquity forever** as a common expression of the culture to mean “keep holding the people’s sins against them and punishing them.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and may you not keep holding our sins against us]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **iniquity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how we have sinned]

10.note: Isaiah is using the possessive form to describe **cities** that are characterized by **holiness**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Your holy cities]

Isaiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Jerusalem has become devastated]

11.note: Isaiah is using the possessive form to describe a **house** that is characterized by **our holiness and our splendor**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Our holy and splendid house]

Isaiah is speaking of the people’s ancestors as if they were their **fathers**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [our forefathers]

Isaiah is using the possessive form to describe a **burning** that is characterized by **fire**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a fiery burning]

12.note: Isaiah is using the question form to appeal to Yahweh not to hold back from helping the people. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [do not restrain yourself, Yahweh!]

Isaiah is using the question form to plead with Yahweh to have mercy and not to keep punishing the people. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Do not remain silent and do not punish us so greatly!]
